items.why: Penalized because the broad negative stem sounds unnatural and merely targets the only negated clause.
Set aside because repeated “he” references blur the distinction between the speaker and the message’s declarer.
Strongly distinguishes the collective victors over all four descendants from the named victor in one battle.
The antecedent of “him” is recoverable and discriminating, though this repeats the trampling event tested by Q299C5.
Distinct saddling and mounting roles make this short actor question highly discriminating.
The explicit first-versus-second covenant contrast cleanly tests two easily confused participant sets.
A clean succession question whose competitor occurs earlier rather than after the burial.
The explicit causal clause separates Uzziah’s own reason for leaving from the priests’ simultaneous action.
The nested plan is worthwhile, but “following the capture of people” is cumbersome and unnatural.
It distinguishes the men’s chosen response from the rejected alternative discussed immediately before it.
Useful chronology across parallel battles, though “who kills first” sounds less natural when the killings occur in separate battles.
Set aside because both “what is later reported” and “the news” are content-poor stand-ins.
The command’s speaker and target have distinct roles, making the actor-object contrast clear.
Clear leader-and-follower roles prevent confusion between Uzziah and the priest leading the group.
The today-versus-tomorrow contrast meaningfully distinguishes which child is planned for each day.
Penalized as simple name lookup because the rival is merely Uzziah’s father from a neighboring sentence.
It precisely distinguishes Elisha’s reply to the doubt from the price prophecy that prompted the doubt.
The stated divine prohibition supplies a complete reason, unlike the incidental size of the offer.
The immediate sequence clearly separates Paul’s prolonged talking from the earlier meal.
The action chain is clear, but identifying its first step adds only modest comprehension value.
The giver-versus-original-owner distinction is both natural and strongly discriminating.
“The addressee” is a technical stand-in that forces unnecessary decoding before the actual role question.
The intended purpose is clear, but “take Amaziah’s son” is an awkward circumlocution for Uzziah.
It tests the command hierarchy rather than confusing the army’s leaders with the officials who mustered it.
The journey sequence resolves the victim cleanly despite two prophets being present in the account.
The wording is clear, but it directly duplicates the stronger antecedent-based trampling question Q89C41.
The dense instructions support a precise contrast between the on-duty and normally off-duty companies.
This compact question cleanly distinguishes the letter’s writer from its recipient.
The rescue scene gives David and Ishbi-Benob sharply distinct roles, making the target unambiguous.
It tests the decision prompted by the men’s moral reassessment rather than an action they had already taken.
Paul’s embedded instruction clearly assigns the message to the young man rather than to Paul.
The immediate sequence cleanly separates the messengers’ report from their earlier pursuit.
The causal attribution is recoverable, but “whose love of soil” is somewhat forced phrasing.
The speaker’s viewpoint and the next-day contrast make the identity of the first child meaningfully discriminating.
The request and response assign distinct roles to the king and the man of God.
It separates the groups opposed with God’s help from the Ammonites, who instead bring tribute.
The route has two nested destinations, so asking for the first one tests sequence rather than mere mention.
“Ahaziah’s son’s nurse” awkwardly encodes the answer through a possessive relationship before asking for it.
The explicit causal clause distinguishes the reason for calm from the accompanying public rejoicing.
It cleanly distinguishes the centurions receiving the order from the soldiers they must assemble.
The hirer and the supposed attackers occupy distinct roles within the Arameans’ mistaken inference.
Resolving “murderer” through the messenger-master relationship yields a strong, nontrivial inference.
The phrase “according to the claim” properly scopes the lie, though it adds slight abstraction to the pronoun test.
The explicit purpose clause supports the reason, while the lamps are clearly incidental.
Penalized because “soldiers” can include the cavalry, weakening the intended group distinction.
The beaten group and the man who overpowers them have clearly opposed roles.
“The items’ arrival” is an unnatural stand-in, and it obscures the contrast between illnesses being cured and spirits leaving.
The petitioners and the official expected to transport Paul have distinct, clearly stated roles.
The sequence is answerable, but “assembling materials” needlessly replaces the concrete action of gathering scrolls.
The woman is also subsequently executed, making the wording less exclusive than the intended order concerning her followers.
It cleanly separates the noise that prompts Athaliah’s movement from the sight she encounters afterward.
The consent-versus-destination contrast is useful, though “must happen” also admits other preparatory steps.
The warning’s addressee and the prophet delivering it are distinct and remain clear through the possessive wording.
The embedded prophecy requires correctly carrying Josiah forward as the subject rather than choosing Jeroboam.
